en.home.cta_band.body: Auth, billing, and email are solved problems. Ship the part that makes you money.
en.home.cta_band.title: Stop rebuilding the same 40%%
en.home.f1.body: Clerk powers sign-in, social OAuth, 2FA, orgs, roles, and invitations — mirrored locally for fast queries.
en.home.f1.title: Auth & teams, hosted
en.home.f2.body: Polar.sh is your merchant of record. Checkout, customer portal, webhooks, and entitlements included.
en.home.f2.title: Billing without tax pain
en.home.f3.body: templ templates, sqlc queries, and Go handlers — the compiler catches what templates usually hide.
en.home.f3.title: Type-safe end to end
en.home.f4.body: No SPA weight. Fragments, toasts, inline validation, and optimistic-feeling tables at ~14 KB.
en.home.f4.title: HTMX interactivity
en.home.f5.body: Strict CSP, CSRF, per-IP rate limiting, hashed API tokens, and auto-escaped templates.
en.home.f5.title: Secure by default
en.home.f6.body: Postgres job queue, audit log, structured logs, Sentry + PostHog hooks, /healthz and /readyz.
en.home.f6.title: Operable from day one
en.home.faq.a1: One static binary, no node in production, no hydration cost. HTMX + Alpine cover the interactivity a SaaS dashboard actually needs.
en.home.faq.a2: Not to evaluate: DEV_AUTH_BYPASS runs the full app locally with zero SaaS accounts. Connect real services when you are ready to ship.
en.home.faq.a3: Yes. Every external service sits behind one narrow Go interface — swapping a provider means replacing one file.
en.home.faq.a4: Strict CSP, CSRF, rate limiting, migrations on boot, background jobs, audit log, tests, CI, and a Dockerfile ship in the box.
en.home.faq.a5: Tailwind v4 standalone CLI and vendored JS — there is no node_modules anywhere in the shipped artifact.

operations.summary: List projects for the token's organization.
operations.description:
Newest first. Two pagination modes share one response shape:

- **`cursor` (preferred)** — keyset paging. Follow `next_cursor` from
  the previous response. Stable under concurrent writes: a cursor
  names a row, so projects created while you page do not shift rows
  across page boundaries, and depth costs nothing server-side.
- **`offset` (legacy)** — the original contract, still honoured. It
  repeats or drops rows when the set changes mid-walk.

`next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque: echo
them back verbatim, never parse or construct them.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Values outside 1–100 fall back to the default.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque position from a previous response's `next_cursor`.
Takes precedence over `offset`. A malformed value is rejected
with 400 rather than silently restarting at the first page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Legacy. Rows to skip; negative values are treated as 0. Ignored
when `cursor` is supplied.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

info.title: GoGoGadget API
info.summary: Bearer-authenticated JSON API for projects and metered AI chat.
info.description:
The second transport. Every rule the HTML app enforces (plan limits,
validation, org scoping) applies identically here — the handlers share
the same query layer and plan logic, they only differ in how they answer.

Authentication is a Bearer token minted at `/app/settings/api`
(`ggg_…`, SHA-256 hashed at rest, shown once). Tokens carry a scope:
`read` satisfies read operations, `write` satisfies both.

The token determines the organization — there is no org parameter, and a
token can never read another org's rows.

operations.description: Unauthenticated so tooling can fetch the contract before holding a token.
